## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to reason about log rotation, gzipped files, and stream processing with minimal tools.

## Key Concepts
- Globbing and rotated logs
- Stream processing with zcat and cat
- Text extraction with sed/awk
- Data aggregation with awk

# Candidate approach (illustrative)
zcat /logs/web/*.log.gz /logs/web/*.log 2>/dev/null | \
awk -v cutoff="$(date -u -d '4 hours ago' +%s)" 'BEGIN{RS=""; FS=""} /"ts":"/ { if(match($0, /"ts":"([^"]+)"/, m)) {
  cmd="date -u -d \"" m[1] "\" +%s"; cmd | getline t; close(cmd);
  if(t>=cutoff && match($0, /"ip":"([0-9.]+)"/, ip)) { c[ip[1]]++ }
}} END{ for(i in c) print c[i]" ""i }' | \

## Why This Is Asked

Assesses ability to craft a robust log-analysis one-liner that handles mixed compression formats, time-window filtering, and cross-file aggregation using only standard UNIX tools.

## Key Concepts

- Shell file globbing and safe looping over missing files
- Decompression with zcat and streaming with cat
- GNU awk time parsing (mktime, systime, strftime)
- Time-window filtering and hour bucketing
- Sorting deterministic output

## Code Example

```javascript
// Conceptual core approach in a single pipeline
for f in /var/log/app/*.log /var/log/app/*.log.* /var/log/app/*.log.gz; do
  case "$f" in
    *.gz) zcat "$f" ;; *) cat "$f" ;; esac;
done | awk 'BEGIN{now=systime()} /\[[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2} [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}\]/ { if (match($0, /\[([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2}) ([0-9]{2}):([0-9]{2}):([0-9]{2})\]/, d)) { ts = mktime(d[1]" "d[2]" "d[3]" "d[4]" "d[5]" "d[6]); if (ts>=now-12*3600 && /ERROR/) { h=strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:00", ts); c[h]++ } } } END{ for (k in c) print k, c[k] }' | sort
```

questions.explanation:
## Identifying D-State Processes
- Use `ps aux | awk '$8 ~ /^D/ {print $2, $11}'` to filter processes in uninterruptible sleep
- Check `/proc/<pid>/status` for detailed process state information
- Monitor system-wide D-state processes with `top` or `htop` filtered by state

## Root Cause Analysis
- Examine `/proc/<pid>/stack` to identify the specific kernel functions blocking the process
- Use `dmesg | grep -i error` to detect hardware or driver-related issues
- Monitor I/O statistics with `iostat -x 1` to identify storage bottlenecks
- Check `lsblk` and `smartctl` for disk health and controller issues

## Common Causes
- NFS server unavailability or network connectivity issues
- Faulty disk controllers, RAID arrays, or storage drivers
- Hardware failures in storage subsystem (bad sectors, failing drives)
- Memory pressure causing excessive swap activity
- Kernel bugs or incompatible device drivers
- Storage system saturation or filesystem corruption
